description: Rules from spec/90-extensions/c2pa.md: the opt-in bridge that points a record at a C2PA 2.2 manifest (C2P-1..C2P-6). Every vector names the bridge it exercises (CON-28), so an implementation that does not claim it skips them. C2P-7 and C2P-8 are consumer obligations and are exempted in exemptions.json.

vectors.name: c2pa/claim-must-be-an-object
vectors.description: The claim is a pointer object; a bare URN string leaves no room for the location.

vectors.name: c2pa/manifest-is-required
vectors.description: A claim that names no manifest points at nothing; without the URN the record cannot be checked against any manifest.

vectors.name: c2pa/manifest-must-be-a-c2pa-urn
vectors.description: A manifest is identified by C2PA's own URN namespace, not by a URL or a filename.

vectors.name: c2pa/manifest-uuid-must-have-the-uuid-shape
vectors.description: The namespace alone is not an identifier: the UUID component is the part that distinguishes one manifest from another.

vectors.name: c2pa/location-is-required
vectors.description: Whether the manifest travels inside the bytes or beside them changes what the digest covers, so it cannot be left implicit.

vectors.name: c2pa/location-is-embedded-or-external
vectors.description: C2PA defines exactly two storage models for a manifest store; a third label would be a claim no implementation can act on.

vectors.name: c2pa/external-manifest-needs-a-uri
vectors.description: An external manifest that names no location cannot be retrieved, so the claim is unverifiable in principle.

vectors.name: c2pa/external-uri-must-be-absolute
vectors.description: A relative path resolves against the reader's working directory, not against the record's author, so it does not locate anything.

vectors.name: c2pa/embedded-manifest-forbids-a-uri
vectors.description: An embedded manifest has one location — the bytes — and a second, possibly stale location would be a contradictable claim.

vectors.name: c2pa/claim-carries-only-the-three-members
vectors.description: Copying assertions into the record duplicates unsigned prose beside the signed manifest that already contains them.

vectors.name: c2pa/id-is-not-the-c2pa-urn
vectors.description: A UUID cannot be recomputed from the bytes, so promoting it to id would make the record unverifiable by its reader.

vectors.name: c2pa/embedded-manifest-is-accepted
vectors.description: The minimal claim: a URN and the fact that the manifest travels inside the bytes.

vectors.name: c2pa/external-manifest-is-accepted
vectors.description: An external store served as application/c2pa, located by an absolute URI.

vectors.name: c2pa/urn-optional-components-are-accepted
vectors.description: C2PA allows a claim-generator and a version-reason after the UUID, and its claim-generator component may itself contain colons. The bridge stores the URN as C2PA emitted it and parses none of it, so the tail is opaque and accepted.

vectors.name: c2pa/urn-hex-case-is-accepted
vectors.description: C2PA's examples are uppercase, but UUID string representations emitted by libraries (Java's UUID.toString(), for one) are lowercase. The record keeps C2PA's label and never re-cases it, so both are accepted.

vectors.name: c2pa/claim-must-not-be-null
vectors.description: JSON null is not an object and not an absent member: a record that writes the key with no claim is rejected, exactly as the schema types it.

vectors.name: c2pa/a-record-without-the-claim-says-nothing
vectors.description: An unclaimed record for an artifact that happens to carry a manifest is still a core record; the bridge is opt-in, and silence is not a denial.
